tool_input.command: cd node_modules/@guren; ls; grep -rln "_i18n" --include=*.js --include=*.ts . | head; grep -rn "i18n" /dev/null; cat ../../package.json | grep -n "\"" | head -40; cat ../../tests/HomeController.test.ts | head -30
cd lang && rm en/messages.json ja/messages.json && cd .. && git checkout lang/en/messages.json && git status --short

result:
The site now has English and Japanese, a language switcher in the header, and Japanese for first visits from a Japanese browser. `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` pass (7 tests), `guren check` reports 0 failures, and `guren check --i18n` shows both catalogs covering the same 29 keys. I did not run the app or click through the pages in a browser.

- **Switcher and choice:** `POST /locale` takes `{ locale }` (`en` or `ja`) and works for guests and signed-in users. It sets a one-year `locale` cookie and redirects to the path from the `Referer`, or `/` if there is none. Only the path is kept, so the redirect can't leave the site. Any other value, or a missing field, returns 422 with the validation error shape the post form already uses. The code is in `app/Http/Controllers/LocaleController.ts`, `app/Http/Validators/LocaleValidator.ts` and `routes/web.ts`.
- **Browser language:** I turned on `ja` in `src/app.ts` (`i18n.supported`). The framework's built-in detection then checks the cookie first, then `Accept-Language`, so a reader's pick beats their browser and `en` is the default. `_i18n.locale` reports the result.
- **Catalogs:** the spec's keys sit in `lang/{en,ja}/nav.json`, `auth.json` and `posts.json`, so `nav.home` and `posts.new` are keys exactly as the spec writes them. I also added `nav.language`, so the switcher's `aria-label` comes from the catalog too. `lang/ja/messages.json` carries the existing welcome message. The nine spec keys have the Japanese values from your table, plus English text of their own.
- **Header and pages:** `Layout.tsx` gets a Home link, translated labels, and an EN / 日本語 switcher. `posts/Index`, `Show`, `New` and `Edit` read their labels from the catalog, including the errors, placeholders and confirm text. 「記事」 appears only in the catalog.
- **Tests:** I added `tests/LocaleController.test.ts`. It covers the cookie and redirect, the no-`Referer` fallback, rejecting `fr` and a missing field, `Accept-Language: ja`, and a cookie pick beating `Accept-Language`.

Only the header navigation and the posts pages use the catalogs. The home, login, register, dashboard and profile pages still have English text in their bodies, since the request named only the header and posts pages.
